title: The Farewell Discourse
lead: John 13:31–17:26, Jesus's long speech and prayer to his disciples on the night before he died. It follows the pattern of the Bible's farewell speeches, in which a leader facing death comforts his people, gives them commands, warns them of trouble and names a successor.

sections.b: Jacob blesses his sons before he dies (Genesis 49). Moses gives all of Deuteronomy as a farewell, ending with a song and a blessing (Deuteronomy 31–33). Joshua (Joshua 23–24), Samuel (1 Samuel 12) and David (1 Kings 2:1–9) give final charges, and Paul says goodbye to the Ephesian elders (Acts 20:17–38). Jewish writings such as the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs collected deathbed speeches. Common features are the announcement of departure, comfort, commands, warnings of trouble, a successor, and a closing prayer or blessing.
sections.refs: Genesis 49; Deuteronomy 31–33; Joshua 23–24; 1 Samuel 12; 1 Kings 2:1–9; Acts 20:17–38; 2 Timothy 4:6–8
